internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root b-h-m appears only three times, always as the noun 'bahiymah' locked in one phrase 'bahiymat al-anaam' (the beast-stock of the grazing livestock). All three verses treat it as lawful, edible livestock given by God as provision and offered ritually; 5:1 adds the one contrast, distinguishing this permitted livestock from hunted game forbidden while in the sacred state. Because the word never stands alone, never varies in form (only its case ending changes for grammar), and is never a verb, we can describe the lexical item and its context confidently but cannot recover any independent meaning of the root itself. We deliberately reject the classical 'mute/inarticulate beast' sense: nothing in these verses touches speech, sound, or obscurity, and importing it would violate the Quran-internal source policy.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: bhm does NOT entail: (1) any action, event, or predication - no verbal or participial use exists anywhere in the corpus; (2) muteness, silence, inarticulateness, vagueness, or obscurity - no occurrence references voice, speech, or sound, so the classical 'mute beast' etymon is Quran-internally unsupported, not merely unproven; (3) humans, wild animals, or hunted game - the referent is domesticated pastoral stock, explicitly opposed to al-Sayd in 5:1; (4) impurity or prohibition - the default valence is lawful provision, with prohibition entering only via external exception clauses (illaa maa yutlaa, ghayra muhillii l-Sayd) attached to the frame, not to bahiymah; (5) any standalone denotation or distributional range - it is never free of al-anaam and never governs another noun.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: There is no internal counterexample to a single-meaning reading: all three tokens are the same noun in the same construct, so consistency is trivial and evidentially cheap. The strongest adversarial fact is STRUCTURAL, targeting any isolable-nucleus or STRONG grade: 5:1:8:1 embeds bahiymat al-anaam in a bare legal-permission frame (uhillat lakum bahiymatu l-anaam) that strips away the razaqahum/ritual-slaughter scaffolding of 22:28 and 22:34, yet bahiymah contributes no new increment - the surrounding frame supplies all the force. This demonstrates that bahiymah behaves as a stable referential label fixed by collocation, and that the root's own contribution cannot be separated from al-anaam or falsified Quran-internally.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: The strongest competing account is the classical 'bahiymah = the mute/inarticulate beast' nucleus (bhm ~ ibham, obscurity/dumbness). It is rejected as the graded result because (a) it is sourced entirely from lexica/tafsir barred by source policy, and (b) it is Quran-internally invisible - no verse cues muteness or obscurity, every cue concerns edibility, provision, and lawfulness. A second competitor is a partitive/descriptive reading giving bahiymah a live general 'beast/quadruped' head that al-anaam narrows; this is admissible as a possibility but not evidenced, since it presupposes a free lexical value the corpus never exhibits and is indistinguishable, on three identical-collocation tokens, from the thinner lexicalized-class account adopted here.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge: one form (N), one lexeme (bahiymah), one frozen construct (bahiymat al-anaam), one semantic field (lawful edible/ritual livestock-provision), zero verbal or derivational spread, and only case-driven surface variation carrying no semantic load. layer_attribution.derivation: No derivation exists: the root produces no verb, participle, or adjective anywhere in the corpus - a single nominal form (N) with zero morphological spread. Morphological identity across tokens is therefore trivial and cannot support a semantic-identity inference.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: A single lexicalized nominal, bahiymah, attested only in the bound construct bahiymat al-anaam, denoting the class of lawful edible pastoral livestock offered as provision/sacrifice. This class-level value is the graded claim (MODERATE, REPRESENTATIVE).

layer_attribution.reconciliation: No cross-cluster reconciliation was needed: a single cluster partitions all 3 occurrences, and no preliminary disposition was overturned. The lenses agreed without conflict.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The isolable semantic contribution of the root bhm itself is UNRESOLVED / not recoverable Quran-internally: one frozen collocation, no minimal pair, no verbal use, no contrast that separates bhm from al-anaam.
